subject: FirstBank SOC2: SDLC spot-check evidence & action log
messages:
From: Lisa Park <lisa.park@firstbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: FirstBank Audit Team <audit@firstbank.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC2 intake — quick SDLC spot-check for code review / CI / secrets / change control

Ben —

Thanks again for jumping on the intake call this morning. As part of our SOC2 scoping we need a short, focused package that demonstrates your secure SDLC controls for a small set of recent changes. Our assessor wants a compact "spot-check" set (not the full artifact bulk) covering these areas:

- Code review (sample PRs + reviewer traces)
- CI/CD controls (pipeline definitions, runner permissions, sample build logs)
- Secrets management (rotation evidence for ephemeral tokens, KMS usage)
- Change approval trail (who approved changes and timing)

Deadline: can you provide the package by EOD Friday 2029-07-12? If you can’t meet that exact date, an interim bundle by end-of-day Thursday with a follow-up by Friday is fine.

Deliverables — please include the following as attachments or links:
- 3 representative PRs (redacted if needed) with timestamped approvals
- CI pipeline snapshot (yaml/json) and one sample build log showing denied vs allowed runner scopes
- Secret rotation manifest for the last 30 days (UUIDs redacted ok, include rotation timestamps)
- Change approval log extract (CSV) for the date range 2029-06-20 to 2029-07-09

If any of these items are sensitive, send redacted files and a short note explaining the redaction. One-page narrative describing controls + who to contact for deep-dive is helpful.

Appreciate it —
Lisa
(FirstBank SOC2 team)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@firstbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jul 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC2 intake — quick SDLC spot-check for code review / CI / secrets / change control

Lisa —

Thanks for the clear list. We can do a compact package by Friday EOD. I’ll coordinate with Marissa (engineering lead for the services repo) and Evelyn (platform security) to assemble the artifacts.

Plan: 
- Thu 07/11: Marissa will extract the three PRs and a short reviewer chain export; Evelyn will pull CI pipeline snapshot and rotation manifest.
- Fri 07/12 AM: I’ll assemble the CSV extract for change approvals and a one-page narrative.
- Fri 07/12 EOD: Delivery via Google Drive link + email packaging.

Two quick clarifying Qs:
1) Are redactions allowed for commit diffs if they contain customer identifiers? (short answer is yes — redaction acceptable).
2) For the "change approval log" do you need the full workflow (Jira + internal approvals) or just the commit-to-approval CSV? We can provide both but the CSV is far smaller.

Marking this high priority. CC'ing Jordan for visibility on any query about the pipeline snapshot.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SOC2 intake — quick SDLC spot-check for code review / CI / secrets / change control

Ben / team —

I pulled candidate PRs from services-repo that match the assessor's ask. Short notes:

- PR #1142 (2029-06-21): feature flag change; reviewers: evelyn.h (security), k.iyer; merge approved by code-owner.
- PR #1187 (2029-06-30): hotfix; reviewers: s.ahmed; had a canary rollback note.
- PR #1203 (2029-07-03): refactor; reviewers: marissa.c, j.blake.

Attached: "code_review_sample.csv" (columns: pr_number, author, reviewers, timestamps, merge_commit). I redacted customer-identifying diffs and replaced with "[REDACTED-DIFF]" tokens.

Evelyn — I need the pipeline snapshot and rotation manifest. For the build log sample pick one successful and one denied-runner event to show permission enforcement. Also include the OIDC role mapping snippet (we have to show ephemeral runner identity mapping).

I’ll prepare a one-paragraph description of the code review policy and the deviation/rollback process to include in the narrative.

Attachments referenced: code_review_sample.csv (attached), PR_links.txt (internal links to PRs).

-M
Marissa Cole
Engineering Lead, Services Repo

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Jul 2029 13:15:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SOC2 intake — quick SDLC spot-check for code review / CI / secrets / change control

Team —

Attached files (shared to folder; attachments also zipped for email delivery):
- ci_pipeline_snapshot-20290710.pdf  (pipeline YAML + brief notes on runner permissions and scopes)
- secret_rotation_manifest-20290709.json  (rotation events for ephemeral tokens and KMS reference IDs; sensitive fields redacted)
- build_log_sample-20290709.txt  (one successful run + one blocked run showing permission enforcement)
- change_approval_log-20290711.csv  (CSV export filtered to 2029-06-20..2029-07-09)

Quick summary:
- CI runners are ephemeral (short-lived OIDC tokens); runner identity mapping to GCP service accounts is enforced by the runner controller.
- Secrets are stored in KMS-backed vault; ephemeral secrets rotate automatically every 7 days for build agents; rotation manifest shows timestamps and rotated key IDs.
- Change approvals are logged in the approvals service and cross-referenced with PR merges (CSV contains commit -> approval_id -> approver -> timestamp).

Ben — I uploaded these to the Drive folder Ben will share externally. Let me know if you want a sanitized version of the build logs.

-Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Platform Security

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Lisa Park <lisa.park@firstbank.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Jul 2029 16:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Delivery: compact SDLC spot-check package for FirstBank SOC2 intake

Lisa —

Per your request, attached is a compact spot-check package that demonstrates our secure SDLC controls. Contents (high level):

- code_review_sample.csv — three representative PRs with reviewer chains; diffs redacted for PII.
- ci_pipeline_snapshot-20290710.pdf — pipeline definition excerpt + runner permissions explanation.
- build_log_sample-20290709.txt — one successful build and one blocked runner event.
- secret_rotation_manifest-20290709.json — rotation timestamps for ephemeral tokens and KMS reference IDs (sensitive identifiers redacted).
- change_approval_log-20290711.csv — commit-to-approval mapping for 2029-06-20..2029-07-09.
- narrative.txt (one page) — control descriptions, exceptions policy, and contact points for deeper dives.

Delivery link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB7-example-FirstBank-SDLC (I also attached a zipped package to this email). Password: sent via 2FA to your audited contact on record.

Action log (internal):
- 2029-07-10 10:05 ben.carter: intake acknowledged, owners assigned.
- 2029-07-11 08:22 marissa.cole: PR sample extracted and redacted.
- 2029-07-11 13:15 evelyn.hart: CI snapshot + rotation manifest uploaded.
- 2029-07-12 16:45 ben.carter: package assembled and delivered to FirstBank.

If you need any additional artifacts or would like a live walkthrough of the pipeline enforcement, Marissa and Evelyn are available for a short session.

Thanks —
Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer — Redwood Inference
